title: G Major Scale (F-sharp)
description: The G major scale introduces the first key signature: one sharp, F-sharp. Same fingering as C major, hands separately, in quarters and then eighths.

arrangements.label: Intermediate
arrangements.notes: RH G4-G5 and LH G2-G3, fingering identical to C major (RH 1-2-3-1-2-3-4-5, LH 5-4-3-2-1-3-2-1); the sharp in the key signature means every F is F-sharp.
teachingPoints: The key signature has one sharp on the F line: play F-sharp (the black key) every time, even though no sharp sign appears in the bar.
RH fingering is the same as C major; finger 4 lands on the black key F-sharp - keep the hand slightly forward so the 4th finger reaches it comfortably.
LH: finger 2 plays F-sharp going up and down; the crossing (thumb on D, 3 on E) is on white keys.
Bars 9-12 in eighths: listen for the leading-tone F-sharp pulling up to G at the top of the scale.
